analysis.subject: civics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers the origin, proposal and ratification of the Bill of Rights, including opponents' demand for protections, congressional proposal, and the fate of the original amendments.

overview.headline: How proposals became the bill of rights and later amendments

keyPoints.point: Students learn that 12 amendments were originally proposed and 10 were ratified to become the Bill of Rights in 1791.
keyPoints.quote: Although 12 amendments were originally proposed, the 10 that were ratified became the Bill of Rights in 1791.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the amendments defined citizens' rights in relation to the newly established government.
keyPoints.quote: They defined citizens' rights in relation to the newly established government under the Constitution.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that opponents repeatedly charged that the Constitution would open the way to tyranny by the central government.
keyPoints.quote: its opponents repeatedly charged that the Constitution as drafted would open the way to tyranny by the central government.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that Articles 3 to 12 were ratified on December 15, 1791 by three-fourths of the state legislatures to constitute the first 10 amendments.
keyPoints.quote: Articles 3 to 12, ratified December 15, 1791, by three-fourths of the state legislatures, constitute the first 10 amendments of the Constitution,

keyTerms.gloss: First 10 amendments ratified to protect rights and define limits on government
keyTerms.quote: Although 12 amendments were originally proposed, the 10 that were ratified became the Bill of Rights in 1791.

keyTerms.gloss: Written plan for the newly established government that defines citizen relations
keyTerms.quote: They defined citizens' rights in relation to the newly established government under the Constitution.

keyTerms.gloss: Abuse of power by a central government feared as tyranny by opponents
keyTerms.quote: its opponents repeatedly charged that the Constitution as drafted would open the way to tyranny by the central government.

keyTerms.gloss: Formally approved by state legislatures after being ratified by the required share
keyTerms.quote: Articles 3 to 12, ratified December 15, 1791, by three-fourths of the state legislatures, constitute the first 10 amendments of the Constitution,

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Helps students order proposal and ratification actions in the taught sequence
componentPlan.focusQuote: On September 25, 1789, the First Congress of the United States therefore proposed to the state legislatures 12 amendments to the Constitution

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Reinforces key facts about rights, proposals and ratification for recall
componentPlan.focusQuote: Although 12 amendments were originally proposed, the 10 that were ratified became the Bill of Rights in 1791.
